- **The systems and versions of other programs.** A 1.x may need a newer Claude Code,
  Git or operating system when older ones stop working; the changelog says so.
- **Variables for testing** that the documentation does not give.

## One exception: security

If fixing a security problem means breaking something on the list, it is fixed in a 1.x,
and the changelog says so first, with what you have to do.

## How it is checked

What can be checked is frozen in files inside the repository, and the tests fail when a
version takes away or changes something in them: the MCP tools with their parameters and
which ones a call must give, the commands with their options and the events of `hook`,
and the settings of each configuration file. Adding is fine. For the notes, every change
of format ships with its step and a test that runs it on notes written the old way, and
in every change the two versions before it must read everything the new one writes.


---

Source: https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting


Something is off. Start here: open a terminal and run

```bash
augmented-brain doctor
```

It checks the whole setup and says what is missing and how to fix it. Each line starts
with a mark: `✓` fine, `·` for your information, `!` a warning, `✗` something that
fails. Under a line that needs work, `→` says what to do.

If you have the panel open, its **Help** page has links to these answers and a button to
report a problem on GitHub, with the health check filled in and what is personal taken
out. See [The panel](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/panel.html#help).

## Problems and fixes

### Claude does not know my tasks, or skips the interview

- **Claude Code asked whether you trust the folder.** The first time you open Claude in
  a folder, Claude Code asks this before loading anything. Say yes in your work folders.
  Until then, augmented brain cannot load your notes.
- **The session started before the install.** Start a new session.
- **You are in another space.** Run `augmented-brain space` in that folder. Outside every
  space's folder, the default space is used. To make a folder count for a space, add it
  to the space's `work_folders` (see [Spaces](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/spaces.html)).

### The terminal cannot find a command

`command not found`, or "not recognized" on Windows. Close the terminal and open a new
one: the one you used does not see the new PATH yet.

### Claude Code stops every command and file change

The guard cannot run, so Claude Code stops everything instead of letting it through. The
program is missing or broken. Run `augmented-brain doctor`. Make sure `augmented-brain`
is on your PATH or in `~/.local/bin`. Installing again fixes it.

### Every PowerShell command is stopped

That is expected, on Windows. The guard reads the shell, not PowerShell, so it stops
PowerShell commands and Claude runs them in Git Bash instead.

### Claude asks before every aws or ssh command

The configuration cannot be read, so the guard does not know your lists and asks to be
safe. `augmented-brain doctor` names the problem. If it says "unknown settings", the
file has a line this version does not know: a typo, or a setting of a newer version. For
a newer version's setting, update with `augmented-brain update`. For a typo, or a change
that broke it, go back to a version that worked: `augmented-brain config history`, then
`augmented-brain config restore <number>`. Both work while the file is broken. See
[Configuration](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/configuration.html) and [Configuration versions](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/config-history.html).

### Claude cannot push, even when I ask

If it says a repository is **untouchable**, that is on purpose: only you can change it, in
the panel's Guard page (see [The guard](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/guard.html#repositories-claude-must-never-touch)).

The guard stops `git commit` and `git push` unless the repository is listed. Push it
yourself, or add the repository to `git_allowed_repos` (or `git_ask_repos`) and ask Claude
to use `git -C <repo>`. See [The guard](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/guard.html#let-claude-commit-in-a-repository).

### Claude asks before a push it used to do

The guard's lists changed outside the panel since you last accepted them (by hand, with a
command, or going back to a version). Until you accept them in the Guard page or start a
new session, a commit, push or merge they allow asks first. `doctor` says so. Open the
panel's Guard page, look at what changed and accept. See [The guard](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/guard.html#only-you-change-the-guards-lists).

### Claude needs root on a machine

Claude gives you the exact command to run yourself. For a migration that needs many
commands, add a dated exception, `root_ask = ["db01 until 2026-12-31"]`. Then root on
that machine asks you each time, until the date.

### augmented brain's tools fail after an update

A session that was open keeps the old program. `augmented-brain session restart --old`
restarts the idle ones, with the same conversation; one of Claude Desktop stays open and
only its augmented brain restarts (on Windows, close and open it). `augmented-brain doctor` says how many sessions still run the old version.

### The installer or the update cannot download

GitHub sometimes fails to hand out a release's files for a while. The installer and
`augmented-brain update` try three times, and also through GitHub's API, which often
keeps working when the usual address does not. If all of it fails, they say so and
nothing changes: the program you had stays. Try again in a while.

What `augmented-brain update` may end with:

- **"cannot reach GitHub to see the latest version"**: `update` asks for the latest
  version once, before downloading. Try again in a while.
- **"the program is still X, not Y"**: the installer ran but the program did not change.
  Nothing else changed; run `augmented-brain update` again later.
- **"The backup failed, so nothing was updated"**: fix the backup (see below) and update
  again, or run `augmented-brain update --force`.

See [Installing](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/install.html#updating).

### The install stopped half way

Run the install command again (or `augmented-brain init`): until it finishes, there is no
configuration, so it starts over. See [Installing](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/install.html).

### "Written by a newer augmented brain"

A newer version on another computer moved the notes to a new format. Update this
computer too: `augmented-brain update`. The older program refuses the notes instead of
breaking them.

### The backup failed

Claude tells you at the start of the next session. Run `augmented-brain backup` in a
folder of the space to see why:

- **No network, or no access.** Check you can reach the repository. On GitHub, log in
  with `gh auth login`.
- **"Stopped after 3m0s without an answer".** The network or the repository did not
  answer, so the backup gave up instead of waiting for good. Try again when the network
  works; the next backup does not wait behind this one.
- **"Another backup has been running for over 10m0s".** A backup that no longer
  answers is in the way. Try again later.
- **A secret in a note.** It names the file. Take the secret out, then back up again.
  `augmented-brain check` names those files too.
- **Two machines changed the same note.** It names the notes, and the folder where to
  merge them by hand. When each machine only added journal entries, they are joined by
  themselves.
- **A file over 50 MB.** It is left out, and the rest is backed up. Move it out of the
  notes folder.

### `doctor` says a space has no backup

If this computer is lost, so are that space's notes. Ask Claude "set up the backup" in a
folder of the space. Or run `augmented-brain backup setup <address of a private
repository>` there, and then `augmented-brain backup`. See [Backup and restore](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/backup.html).

### A note is not valid

`augmented-brain check` in a folder of the space lists each problem with its file. Fix
the header (between the `---` lines) by hand, and run `check` again. Until then, the
index is not rebuilt, but the tools keep working.

A file that cannot be read (its permissions, or a broken link left by a sync) is listed
the same way: fix its permissions, or move it out of the notes folder. A file whose name
starts with a dot, such as the lock file Emacs leaves while you edit a note, is skipped.

### A repository is "not on this computer"

A task names a repository in `repos:` that is in none of the space's work folders. It
was moved, renamed or deleted, or this computer never had it. Tell Claude where it is
now, or remove it from the task.

### Claude Code keeps a second memory

`doctor` warns that Claude Code keeps a memory of its own for your folders. It drifts
from the space's. Add `"autoMemoryEnabled": false` to the settings file `doctor` names.
What it holds stays, and you can [bring it in](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/import.html).

### Other users can read my notes

`doctor` warns about it. Run `augmented-brain check` in a folder of the space: it makes
the notes yours only.

### The panel does not open, or its address stopped working

On a computer with no screen, `augmented-brain panel` prints the address to open
yourself. That address works once, within 2 minutes. The pages it opens carry a key
that changes each time the panel starts, and the panel stops after 30 minutes without
use. Run `augmented-brain panel` again for a new address. If your browser says "This
link was already used" and you did not open it, something else did: look at the
panel's Guard page.

### The panel from another device does not open

`doctor` says what is missing: Tailscale stopped, HTTPS off in your network, or an
address left published after the panel stopped (it gives the command to remove it). See
[The panel from another device](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/panel-remote.html).

### Remote access does not work

Run `augmented-brain remote status`: under each problem, `→` says what to do. Usually
Claude does not trust the folder yet (run `cd <folder> && claude` once), or linger is
off. `remote install` stops, changing nothing, on a machine without systemd's user
services (a container, WSL without systemd). See [Remote access](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/remote.html).

### A session was cut off

The window was closed by force, or the computer went down. The next session offers to
recover it. Say yes, or use the panel: Today lists it. Claude Code keeps each
conversation for 30 days.

### The window uses a lot of memory

Claude says that the window uses a lot of memory, or `doctor` warns about a Claude window
of several GB. The process that holds the window's sessions has grown far past normal:
VS Code's extension host (the program inside VS Code that runs Claude and the other
extensions), or Claude itself in a terminal. It normally stays near 0.5 GB for days.
Now and then one grows without stopping, and the system ends up closing it, with every
Claude session of the window. The length of the conversation has nothing to do with it.

What to do, as soon as you see it:

1. Ask Claude to park the task ("park it"). Where you were and what comes next are kept.
2. Open a new VS Code window (or a new terminal session) and resume the task there.
3. Close the old window when you are done with it: that frees the memory.

Claude warns at 2 GB, then at 4 and 8 GB, once each. On Windows it does not look.

### Old worktrees and scratch folders pile up

`doctor` says that something was left over from working with Claude Code. When Claude
Code works in a worktree (a second working copy of a repository, in `.claude/worktrees`),
the worktree stays after the session ends. Its sessions also leave scratch folders in
the system's temporary folder, which a computer that is rarely restarted never empties.

Run `augmented-brain clean`. It shows what it would remove and asks first. A worktree with
changes, commits or ignored files (a `.env`) of its own is never removed: it only names
it, so you look at it.

### After a restore, nothing asks before production

Backups do not carry the guard's lists. Open a Claude session: it offers to ask you for
them. Or add `production_aws_profiles` and `untouchable_hosts` to the configuration
yourself.

### After a restore, secrets "could not be checked"

The keychain could not be asked: a Linux machine without a desktop session, a locked
macOS keychain, or Windows, where it cannot be asked. The secrets may be there. Open a
desktop session or unlock the keychain, and look in the panel's Secrets page. Store those
that are missing with the command shown. See [Backup and restore](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/backup.html).

### Windows: accents look broken (`sesiÃ³n`)

Windows PowerShell 5.1 misreads what other programs write when it captures it. The text
is right: in Git Bash, or in a window, it shows well.

### macOS: the developer tools window did not open

Run `xcode-select --install`, then the install command again.

More problems of the installer, on each system: [Installing](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/install.html#if-something-goes-wrong).

## Questions

### Is it free?

augmented brain is: open source, MIT license, no account, no subscription. But it works
with Claude Code, which needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or above).

### Do my notes leave my computer?

augmented brain never sends them anywhere. But your assistant reads them to work, like
any file it opens, so they travel with the conversation to its provider. With a backup,
they also go to the private repository you chose.

### Can I edit the notes by hand?

Yes, they are Markdown files. Afterwards, run `augmented-brain check`.

### Which assistants does it work with?

Claude Code today. The tools are an MCP server, an open standard, so other assistants can
follow.

### What if I stop using it?

Your notes stay where they are, as plain files. There is nothing to export. See
[Installing](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/install.html#uninstalling).

## Still stuck

Tell us in [the project's issues](https://github.com/icalvete/augmented-brain/issues),
with what showed up on screen and what `augmented-brain doctor` says. The panel's Help
page fills that in for you.

What changed in each version is in the
[changelog](https://github.com/icalvete/augmented-brain/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).


---

Source: https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/limitations.html

# Known limitations


What augmented brain cannot do yet, or does only in part. Each line says what to do
instead. The list grows when something new turns up: if you find one, tell us from the
panel's Help page.

## Only Claude Code

augmented brain works with Claude Code: the terminal, the desktop app and the IDE
extensions. Other assistants could use the note tools over MCP, but the session start
and the guard rely on Claude Code's hooks, so they would get neither.

## Windows

- **Claude runs commands in Git Bash, not in PowerShell.** The guard reads the commands
  of a POSIX shell (Bash), not PowerShell, so it stops every PowerShell command, and
  Claude uses Git Bash instead. What only works in PowerShell, you run yourself: Claude
  gives you the command. When Claude tries PowerShell anyway, you see a red
  `PreToolUse:PowerShell hook error`: that is the guard stopping it, and Claude goes on
  in Bash. Nothing is wrong.
- **Installing over ssh asks nothing.** In an ssh session Windows says nobody is at the
  keyboard, so the installer cannot ask: it prints the commands to run instead, and winget
  often fails there. Install from PowerShell on the desktop, or with `AB_YES=1` to answer
  yes to everything.
- **Accents can look broken** (`sesiÃ³n`) in Windows PowerShell 5.1. The fix is in
  [Troubleshooting](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/troubleshooting.html).

## Claude Code's first run

The first time you run `claude`, Claude Code shows its own screens before augmented
brain says anything: a colour theme, your sign-in, and whether you trust the folder.
In your space, answer **Yes, I trust this folder**: Enter alone picks "No, exit". Ctrl-C
does not leave the theme screen; pick one with Enter. These screens belong to Claude
Code, and augmented brain cannot change them.

## Remote access and a session per task

`augmented-brain remote` (reaching your computer from claude.ai or Claude Desktop) works
on Linux, macOS and Windows. `augmented-brain session start` (a remote session for one
task) works on Linux only for now: on macOS and Windows it says so and changes nothing.

- **On a Mac and on Windows, remote access starts when you log in**, not before. After a
  restart, including one the computer does by itself (an update, a power cut), nobody
  can connect until you log in once. On Linux it can start with nobody logged in.
- **On Windows it runs only while you are logged in.** If you sign out, it stops.
- **On Windows, a folder with `%` in its name** may keep remote access from starting
  there. Pick another folder with `folders` in `remote.toml`.
- **A real connection has been tried on Linux only.** On a Mac and on Windows, install,
  status and uninstall are tested in CI with a pretend Claude; connecting from claude.ai
  has not been tried yet.
- A session opened with `session start` does not come back after a reboot: ask for it
  again. The space's own remote session does.
- Claude allows one remote session per folder, and the folder must be trusted on its
  own. `session start` tells you what to do the first time.

## macOS

Every pull request runs the tests on a Mac in CI, including the installer, Safari and a
locked keychain. A few things only a person at a real Mac can see, and nobody checks
them yet:

1. Opening the program downloaded with a browser from the Finder ("Open Anyway").
2. A real Claude Code session: the guard stops a push and the session start loads.
3. Claude Desktop installed by the installer, and Tailscale with `panel remote`.
4. With no network: `backup`, `update` and `panel remote` say so and leave nothing half
   done.
5. The panel in Safari with its console open, free of errors.

If one of them fails for you, no one has seen it yet: please report it.

## The guard

The guard reads each command as text before Claude runs it. It catches the mistakes an
assistant makes; it is not a wall, and it does not replace permissions, backups or your
own review. What it cannot see:

- **Scripts written by another program.** If Claude writes a script with a program
  (Python, a build tool) and runs it later, the guard only sees what the script holds
  when it runs. A script written and run in the same command is checked; one written in
  a way the guard cannot read makes it ask you first.
- **Values known only when the command runs.** When a program or a folder comes from a
  variable or from another command's output, the guard cannot know it in advance: it
  asks you, but it cannot tell you exactly what will run.
- **Settings changed through a program.** The guard asks before Claude edits augmented
  brain's or Claude Code's settings with its file tools or common commands. A small
  program written on the spot (in Python, say) could still change them; the guard
  notices afterwards and asks before a commit or a push, but it does not prevent it.
  Such a program could also use the panel with a link it saw: the link works once, so
  your browser would say it was already used, and Claude Code tells you what the panel
  changed.
- **Git aliases in included files.** Your git aliases count as what they stand for
  (`git ci` for `git commit`) when they are in your usual git settings. An alias in a
  file those settings `include` is not seen.
- **Local commits from merge, revert and cherry-pick.** The guard stops `git commit`
  where Claude may not commit, but `git merge`, `git revert` and `git cherry-pick` also
  make commits on your computer. They are not published: a push is still stopped.
- **Rules Claude saves.** Claude saves a rule, your profile or a host for the guard
  without asking you first, and every later session loads them. A text Claude read (a
  web page, an email) could talk it into saving one. Nothing stops that, but you are
  told: Claude Code itself shows you, once, what was saved. If you did not ask for it,
  tell Claude to undo it, or look at the panel.
- **Questions in automatic modes.** When the guard asks, Claude Code shows you the
  question. What Claude Code does with it in its fully automatic modes is up to Claude
  Code, not augmented brain.

More in [The guard](https://icalvete.github.io/augmented-brain/guide/guard.html).

## Tested by few people

augmented brain is beta. One person has used it every day on Ubuntu, and tried it on
macOS and Windows 11. What you have keeps working from one version to the next (see the
[disclaimer](https://github.com/icalvete/augmented-brain/blob/main/DISCLAIMER.md)), but
back up anything important.
